column1: # Claims made on the fork landing page, and the test that proves each one.
# No claim without a test: scripts/fork-proof.sh fails if a claim here has no
# matching test, or if its test does not actually fail against upstream. A claim
# that upstream has since fixed will start passing there — delete the row and the
# corresponding fork divergence. See CONTEXT.md, "Claim" and "Proof suite".
#   fidelity   upstream drops information, the fork keeps it (output gets LARGER)
#   reduction  upstream passes output through unfiltered, the fork filters it

column3: Upstream filters `git --porcelain` output that was never meant to be read by a human; the fork passes machine output through byte-for-byte.
Upstream aborts (SIGABRT, exit 134) on any argument containing non-UTF-8 bytes, before the wrapped command runs; the fork executes it.
The wrapped tool receives the exact bytes the user typed, not a lossy copy.
A non-UTF-8 argument to a command that does not exist exits cleanly instead of aborting.
Upstream discards the error output of a failed `pnpm install`; the fork preserves it.
Upstream swallows a failing tool's stderr under stdout-only filtering; the fork surfaces it.
